topic: SQL vs NoSQL: PostgreSQL or MongoDB for your product
caption:
PostgreSQL or MongoDB? Your database choice is easy to make and hard to undo. 🗄️

The founder's version:

✅ SQL (PostgreSQL, MySQL) when your data is connected: users, orders, payments, reports
✅ NoSQL (MongoDB, DynamoDB) when your data is flexible or document-shaped, or you need simple scaling for high volume
✅ Decide on how your data relates and how you'll query it, not on what's trending

Swipe for the details. →

Not sure which fits your product? DM us DATA with a one-line description and we'll tell you what we'd pick and why.

slides.title: SQL or NoSQL: which database does your product need?
slides.sub: Easy to choose, hard to undo. Swipe →

cols.name: SQL
cols.text: Tables with clear relationships. Strong consistency and powerful queries for connected data.

cols.name: NoSQL
cols.text: Flexible documents or key-value items. Easy to evolve and scale for simple, high-volume access.

slides.title: Choose SQL when…
slides.body: your data is connected: users, orders, payments, inventory and reports that all reference each other. That's most business apps.

slides.title: Choose NoSQL when…
slides.body: your data is flexible or document-shaped, like content, events or logs, and you read it in predictable ways at high volume.

slides.title: Don't decide on hype.
slides.body: Decide on how your data relates and the questions you'll ask it. Many products use both, each where it fits.
